clue.text: Finished, having fallen over, caught in fight, after this?

definitions.text: Finished, having fallen over, caught in fight, after this?

indicators.note: something that has fallen over is upside down, so in a down-reading sense the word for finished is turned back to front

parts.note: a game that is up is over and finished

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught is placed inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a night that ended in a punch-up and asks what led to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having fallen over' reverses the word for finished, and 'in' places the cricket abbreviation inside the fight. The whole clue also hints that a drunken tour of bars so often ends in a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of several bars drinking at each is the classic prelude to a late-night fight.

clue.text: I don't know success

definitions.meaning: what a quiz contestant says when declining to answer
getting through an exam or test

explanation.definitionFit: Pass is the quiz-show word for declining a question and also a successful exam result.

clue.text: Cry when upset, given onion

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: blub is an informal word for cry

explanation.surface: Someone weeps after being handed an onion to chop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns BLUB over in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a bulb, the swollen underground storage organ of the plant.

clue.text: Being a contender, Bill boxing?

annotationWithheld.why: Being a contender, Bill boxing? (6) for RACING: AC (bill) inside RING needs 'boxing' to give RING and also signal the container, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: White stuff — with it something with pong wrapped in toilet paper

indicators.note: the two pieces are enclosed by the abbreviation for a toilet

parts.note: WC stands for water closet, a toilet
hip means fashionable or with it
ping goes with pong in the game ping-pong
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A grubby description of something white and smelly in the loo roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pong' is British slang for a bad smell, which steers away from ping-pong. 'wrapped in' puts HIPPING inside WC.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping cream is thick white cream that can be whisked until stiff.

clue.text: Accommodation for soldiers' target area?

parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg, so their target sits in a little holder at the breakfast table rather than a barracks

explanation.walkthrough: Military 'soldiers' and 'target area' point at barracks and firing ranges; in British nursery talk, soldiers are fingers of buttered toast dunked in a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The small cup holding a boiled egg is the target into which toast fingers called soldiers are dipped.

clue.text: Yogdaws?

parts.note: a nonsense word made by scrambling the deity's name and planting it inside a scrambled word for paths, so the saying is acted out literally

explanation.walkthrough: Read the saying as instructions: GOD, scrambled, moves inside a mysterious (anagrammed) WAYS, giving Y-OGD-AWS, the nonsense word printed.
explanation.definitionFit: This proverb about divine providence comes from a William Cowper hymn and is spelled out literally by the clue.

clue.text: Dish having outrageous 19, devout in church

indicators.note: the three pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the Church of England

parts.note: CE is Church of England
OTT means over the top, outrageous
the answer to 19 is a span of time, and age is another word for a long time
pi is informal for pious or devout

explanation.surface: A meal in a church setting is linked with scandalous behaviour and piety.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' refers to entry 19, TIME, of which AGE is a synonym. Cottage pie is a British dish of minced beef topped with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is a baked dish of minced meat under a mashed potato crust.

clue.text: Unquestionable friendship has such features

parts.note: proper can mean genuine, real, beyond question
ties are bonds of friendship

explanation.surface: Real friendship is said to have certain characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Properties are characteristic qualities or features of something.

clue.text: Group about to take office in Jewish nation

indicators.note: the word for one about to take office is placed inside the name for the Jewish nation

parts.note: Sion, a variant spelling of Zion, stands for the Jewish people or homeland
elect after a title, as in president-elect, means chosen but not yet in office

explanation.surface: A party poised to take power in Israel is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to take office' reads like a separate time phrase, but it is the whole meaning of ELECT, as in 'president-elect'.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a chosen group or assortment of things or people.

clue.text: Apparent success in destruction of nature without a consequence thereof?

indicators.note: the charade goes inside the wrecked letters
destroyed letters are broken up and rebuilt in another order
the article is taken out of the word nature

parts.note: clear means apparent or obvious
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A seeming victory amid environmental devastation brings an ugly aftermath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from nature, 'destruction of' rearranges what is left, and 'in' puts the apparent success inside it. The definition looks back to the nuclear destruction the surface implies.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolonged dark freezing period is predicted to follow a nuclear war as a consequence of the destruction.

clue.text: Again what should hold it together?

annotationWithheld.why: Again what should hold it together? (5) for DITTO: no sound parse found; DO (abbreviation of ditto) holding IT + TO would need 'what should' to give DO and 'together' to give TO, neither of which holds
annotationWithheld.clue: Again what should hold it together?

clue.text: Office where Prescott alien to work left to be dismissed

indicators.note: set to work, the letters of the remaining words are reorganised into a new order
dismissed means sent away, so the abbreviation for left is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: John Prescott, a Labour deputy prime minister, finds his department hostile ground as the left is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be dismissed' removes the L from PRESCOTTALIEN, and 'to work' rearranges the remaining twelve letters. John Prescott was Britain's deputy prime minister when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is a government office or body of officials charged with inspecting.

clue.text: Cast containing goody-goody good as a ropey show in the main

definitions.text: as a ropey show in the main

indicators.note: the word for cast holds the two pieces inside

parts.note: shied means threw or cast
a prig is a self-righteous goody-goody

explanation.surface: Actors portraying smug characters stage a feeble play at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropey' means shoddy in British slang, but here it means full of ropes; 'the main' is the sea. 'Cast' tempts as a theatre cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship-rigged vessel carries square sails on three masts, a showy array of ropes on the high seas.

clue.text: Grace holds content of Christmas cracker up, yawning

indicators.note: the grace word keeps the turned-round piece inside it

parts.note: to say grace is to bless food

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a motto, a joke or saying on paper, is found inside a Christmas cracker

explanation.surface: Grace is bored while finding the slip inside her Christmas cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MOTTO into OTTOM, held in BLESS. A Christmas cracker is a British party novelty, a tube pulled apart to release a hat, toy and motto.
explanation.definitionFit: Yawning in the sense of gaping wide open, like an abyss that seems to have no bottom.

clue.text: Laugh is a blast

definitions.meaning: the sound of a car horn or owl's call, or a very funny thing or occasion

explanation.definitionFit: Hoot means both a burst of laughter and a short blast on a horn or whistle.

clue.text: Bet has to give up, not disheartened given earlier event

parts.note: an ante is the stake put into the pot in poker
to cede is to give up or surrender

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its first and last letters here

explanation.surface: A gambler forced to surrender a stake stays cheerful in the face of something that happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips the middle O out of 'not', leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An antecedent is something that came before, a preceding event or circumstance.

clue.text: In favour of drink, quarter abandoned

parts.note: for means supporting or in favour of
sake is a Japanese rice wine
N, north, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone who backs drinking gets left behind in a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means deserted or left behind entirely.

clue.text: Pandas clasp at last of bamboo, right pair suffering

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of order
only the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: two copies of R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Giant pandas grab the end of a bamboo stalk while a couple of them look unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes O from bamboo; 'suffering' rearranges CLASPAT + O + RR. Panda cars were British police patrol cars, once painted in black-and-white or blue-and-white blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain police patrol vehicles were nicknamed panda cars for their two-tone paint.

clue.text: See 23
In a rut, fake fur

indicators.note: fake things are not the genuine article, so these letters are forged into another order

explanation.surface: Stuck in a routine, someone wears imitation fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' rearranges the letters of 'In a rut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutria is the fur of the coypu, a South American rodent.

clue.text: See 6
See 6
For now, the evil enemy

parts.note: mean can describe nasty or wicked behaviour
time is often called the enemy, as in time the great enemy

explanation.surface: A temporary villain is identified as the foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Meantime means the intervening period, the present stopgap: for the time being.

clue.text: European railway's first to occupy train spotter, perhaps

indicators.note: the picked letter takes up residence inside the word for an obsessive hobbyist

parts.note: a train spotter is given as an example of a geek, an obsessive enthusiast

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the railway word is used

explanation.surface: A railway enthusiast from the Continent is sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: A train spotter is a British hobbyist who logs locomotive numbers, a byword for nerdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek is a native of Greece, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Many vehicles finding prominence half came into fashion

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for fashion

parts.note: mode means fashion or style
a tor is a rocky hill or prominence, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: only the first two of the word's four letters are used

explanation.surface: A fleet of cars gets noticed for arriving halfway in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first two letters of came. A tor is a rocky hilltop typical of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of many motor vehicles, typically escorting a dignitary.

clue.text: Distributing drugs, seeing vice in midst of plague

indicators.note: the word for vice sits in the middle of the word for plague

parts.note: to dog is to trouble or plague persistently
a sin is a moral fault or vice

explanation.surface: A dealer pushes pills in the middle of an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plague' looks like a noun here, but it is the verb, giving DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosing means giving out doses of medicine, administering drugs.

clue.text: Statesman's creation of Genesis second in articles

parts.note: Noah's ark is built in the Book of Genesis

indicators.note: the abbreviation for second goes between the two articles

parts.note: two indefinite articles, an and an

explanation.surface: A politician produces something from the Bible among a few objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is misleading: read it as a man of a US state, here someone from Arkansas.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arkansan is a native of Arkansas, literally a man of that US state.
